original_title: I usually skip soulslikes not made by FromSoftware, but one Steam demo just won me over
summary_en: A new Steam demo for Prison of Husks is turning heads by embracing a distinct PS1 aesthetic and blending familiar Souls-like mechanics with its own unique twists. This indie title is proving that the genre isn't solely the domain of FromSoftware.
ai_analysis: Prison of Husks' commitment to a retro visual style and tight combat mechanics offers a refreshing take on the soulslike genre, potentially appealing to both genre veterans and newcomers.

en.title: Prison of Husks Demo Wins Over Soulslike Skeptics With Retro Charm
en.summary: A new Steam demo for Prison of Husks is turning heads by embracing a distinct PS1 aesthetic and blending familiar Souls-like mechanics with its own unique twists. This indie title is proving that the genre isn't solely the domain of FromSoftware.
en.body:
For many dedicated fans, the allure of the soulslike genre is inextricably linked to the masterful creations of **FromSoftware**. Titles like **Elden Ring**, **Dark Souls**, and **Bloodborne** have set an incredibly high bar, often making it difficult for other developers to stand out. This has led to a common sentiment among hardcore players: if it's not made by FromSoftware, it's probably best to skip it. However, a recent demo on Steam for a game called **Prison of Husks** is challenging that very notion, captivating players with its bold design choices and surprisingly robust gameplay.

The initial impression of **Prison of Husks** immediately sets it apart. Instead of chasing modern graphical fidelity, the developers have leaned heavily into a distinct retro PS1 rendering style. This isn't just a superficial coat of paint; it's woven into the core experience with a forced 4:3 aspect ratio, a default 640x480 resolution, and chunky, console-inspired menus. These elements combine to create a genuine sense of nostalgia, feeling like an authentic expression of a bygone era rather than a fleeting indie trend.

## A Familiar Yet Fresh Formula

Beneath its retro veneer, **Prison of Husks** skillfully blends elements from beloved FromSoftware titles. The camera work, controls, and overall atmosphere evoke the deliberate pacing and gothic dread found in **Demon's Souls**, while the combat mechanics hint at the precise, reactive style of **Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice**. The developers have managed to capture the essence of what makes these games so compelling, but crucially, they've infused it with enough of their own ideas to forge a distinct identity. The perfect block or parry system, in particular, is a standout feature, encouraging players to master its timing. One reviewer found themselves replaying a miniboss dozens of times just to perfect the parry mechanic, a testament to its satisfying execution.

While the combat feels remarkably solid, it's not without its minor imperfections. There were moments where the window for a meaningful counter-attack after a parry felt a bit tight, and the game lacks the crystal-clear stagger meter feedback that **Sekiro** so effectively employs. Yet, even with these small caveats, the combat feels more engaging and rewarding than that of many other Sekiro-inspired titles encountered. The atmosphere, too, draws players in with its towering, grey gothic structures and the signature cryptic lore that fans have come to expect from the genre, creating a palpable sense of unease and mystery.

## Why This Demo Matters to Fans

For players who, like the original source material's author, typically shy away from non-FromSoftware soulslikes, **Prison of Husks** represents a beacon of hope. It demonstrates that the core appeal of the genre—challenging combat, intricate level design, and atmospheric world-building—can be successfully replicated and even innovated upon by smaller studios. The demo's success on Steam suggests a strong community appetite for games that respect the legacy of the soulslike while daring to experiment. It raises questions about the established biases within the gaming community and highlights the potential for hidden gems to emerge when developers are given the freedom to pursue unique artistic visions.

## What's Next

The demo for **Prison of Husks** is currently available on Steam, offering players a substantial glimpse into the game's world and mechanics. Further details regarding the full release date and platform availability have not yet been announced, but this promising demo has certainly put the game on the radar of many passionate soulslike enthusiasts.

tr.title: Hücre Hapishanesi Demo, Retro Karizmasıyla Soulslike Şüphecilere Kazanıyor
tr.summary: Steam'de yayınlanan Hücre Hapishanesi demo sürümü, benzersiz PS1 estetiği ve Souls-like mekanikleriyle dikkatleri üzerine çekiyor. Bu bağımsız oyun, FromSoftware'in dışındaki geliştiricilerin de soulslike türünde iddialı olabileceğini kanıtlıyor. Demo, soulslike severlerin ilgisini çekerek türün FromSoftware'in tekelinde olmadığına işaret ediyor.
tr.body:
## Soulslike Türünün Yeni Bir Yüzü

FromSoftware'in soulslike oyunları, birçok oyuncunun kalbinde özel bir yere sahiptir. **Elden Ring**, **Dark Souls** ve **Bloodborne** gibi oyunlar, soulslike türünün standardını belirlemiştir. Ancak bu, diğer geliştiricilerin soulslike oyunlar geliştirmesini engellememelidir. **Hücre Hapishanesi** demo sürümü, bu durumu değiştirebilecek potansiyele sahip gibi görünüyor.

## Retro Estetik ve Taze Mekanik

**Hücre Hapishanesi**, ilk bakışta dikkat çekici bir retro PS1 estetiği sunuyor. Geliştiriciler, modern grafik kalitesini takip etmek yerine, bir PS1 oyununun hissiyatını yaratmayı hedeflemişler. 4:3 ekran oranı, 640x480 çözünürlük ve konsol benzeri menüler, oyuna gerçek bir nostaljik hava katıyor. Bu, sadece bir yüzey işlemi değil, oyunun temel deneyimine işlenen bir unsur.

## Tanıdık Ancak Taze Bir Formül

**Hücre Hapishanesi**, FromSoftware'in sevgili oyunlarının unsurlarını ustaca birleştiriyor. Kamera çalışması, kontroller ve genel atmosfer, **Demon's Souls**'un kasten yavaş tempolu ve gotik korkusuyla benzerlik gösteriyor. Savaş mekanikleri ise **Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice**'ın precisa ve reaktif stilini çağrıştırıyor. Geliştiriciler, bu oyunların çekici yanlarını başarılı bir şekilde yakalamışlar, ancak aynı zamanda sufficient sayıda kendi fikirlerini eklemişler. Blok veya parry sistemi, özellikle dikkat çekici bir özellik, oyuncuların zamanlamasını ustaca kullanmasını teşvik ediyor.

## Bu Demo Neden Önemli

**Hücre Hapishanesi**, soulslike türünün sadece FromSoftware'in tekelinde olmadığını gösteriyor. Demo, soulslike severlerin ilgisini çekerek, bu türün çekici yanlarının - zorlu savaş, karmaşık düzey tasarımı ve atmosferik dünya oluşturması - başarılı bir şekilde diğer stüdyolarda da uygulanabileceğini kanıtlıyor. Bu, soulslike severlerin yeni ve heyecan verici deneyimlere açık olabileceğini gösteriyor.

## Sonraki Adımlar

**Hücre Hapishanesi** demo sürümü şu anda Steam'de mevcut ve oyunculara oyunun dünyası ve mekanikleri hakkında kapsamlı bir bakış sunuyor. Tam sürümün yayın tarihi ve platform erişimi hakkında henüz bir açıklama yapılmadı, ancak bu demo, soulslike severlerin radarına girmeyi başardı.

es.title: La demo de Prison of Husks conquista a los escépticos del género Soulslike con su encanto retro
es.summary: Una nueva demo en Steam para Prison of Husks está llamando la atención al adoptar una estética distintiva de PS1 y combinar mecánicas Soulslike familiares con giros únicos. Este título indie está demostrando que el género no es exclusivo de FromSoftware. La demo ofrece una experiencia que recuerda a los clásicos, con un estilo gráfico retro y una jugabilidad sólida que desafía a los jugadores a dominar sus habilidades.
es.body:
Para muchos fanáticos dedicados, el atractivo del género Soulslike está inextricablemente ligado a las creaciones magistrales de **FromSoftware**. Títulos como **Elden Ring**, **Dark Souls** y **Bloodborne** han establecido una barra muy alta, a menudo haciendo que sea difícil para otros desarrolladores destacarse. Sin embargo, una demo reciente en Steam para un juego llamado **Prison of Husks** está desafiando esa noción, cautivando a los jugadores con sus audaces decisiones de diseño y una jugabilidad sorprendentemente robusta.

 
## Una Fórmula Familiar pero Fresca

Bajo su apariencia retro, **Prison of Husks** combina habilmente elementos de títulos queridos de FromSoftware. El trabajo de cámara, los controles y la atmósfera general evocan el ritmo deliberado y el terror gótico encontrado en **Demon's Souls**, mientras que las mecánicas de combate sugieren el estilo preciso y reactivo de **Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice**. Los desarrolladores han logrado capturar la esencia de lo que hace que estos juegos sean tan atractivos, pero crucialmente, han infundido suficientes ideas propias para forjar una identidad distintiva. El sistema de bloqueo o parada perfecto es una característica destacada, alentando a los jugadores a dominar su temporización. Un revisor se encontró repitiendo una miniboss docenas de veces solo para perfeccionar la mecánica de parada, un testimonio de su satisfactoria ejecución.

 
## ¿Por qué esta demo es importante para los fanáticos?

Para los jugadores que, como el autor del material original, suelen evitar títulos Soulslike no desarrollados por FromSoftware, **Prison of Husks** representa una señal de esperanza. Demuestra que el atractivo central del género — combate desafiante, diseño de niveles intrincado y construcción de mundos atmosféricos — puede ser replicado con éxito y hasta innovado por estudios más pequeños. El éxito de la demo en Steam sugiere un fuerte apetito comunitario por juegos que respeten el legado de Soulslike mientras se atreven a experimentar. Plantea preguntas sobre los sesgos establecidos dentro de la comunidad de juegos y resalta el potencial para que surjan joyas ocultas cuando a los desarrolladores se les da la libertad de perseguir visiones artísticas únicas.

 
## Próximos Pasos

La demo de **Prison of Husks** está actualmente disponible en Steam, ofreciendo a los jugadores una visión sustancial del mundo y las mecánicas del juego. No se han anunciado detalles adicionales sobre la fecha de lanzamiento completa y la disponibilidad de plataformas, pero esta prometedora demo ciertamente ha puesto el juego en el radar de muchos entusiastas apasionados de Soulslike.

content_raw: I'm a FromSoft fiend, but there are hardly any other soulslikes I can stand. I can dig something a bit more removed like the first-person Lunacid or 2D Mina the Hollower , but there's an uncanny valley effect for me with stuff like Lies of P or Nioh: It's so close to being the thing I love, but doesn't quite bring it home. Enter Prison of Husks , whose demo is live on Steam: It carries the same risk of comparison to the champaign of Souls with its camera, controls, and vibes, but manages to be different enough to really get my goat. The first thing that won me over was its commitment to a retro PS1 rendering style, boasting little touches that come off as genuine retro expression rather than hopping on an indie trend. Those touches include a forced 4:3 aspect ratio, 640x480 default resolution, and chunky console menus. Through that filter, Prison of Husks looks to be blending Demon's Souls vibes and level design with Sekiro combat, as well as some flourishes all its own. I'm a sucker for a good perfect block parry, and Prison of Husks' had me running back a demo miniboss dozens of times until I buried it. It's not perfect: Sometimes it felt like I didn't have a big enough window to meaningfully counter after a parry, and Prison of Husks lacks the crystal-clear feedback of Sekiro's stagger meter. But the combat felt good—better than most lesser Sekiros I've encountered. As for the atmosphere, I was intrigued. It's the grey, towering gothic structures and specific strain of cryptic "ooh cursed one" that I associate with Demon's Souls and, to a lesser extent, Dark Souls 1. You play as some kind of life-sized doll automaton possessed by a wayward soul⁠—or maybe more accurately, you play as a wayward soul possessing doll automatons⁠—and you really ought to do something about all this entropic curse stuff in the air. Glass Head Dolls Glass Head Dolls Glass Head Dolls Glass Head Dolls Prison of Husks is also trying some mechanical experimentation that I respect: It's leaning more action/exploration than RPG, with equippable gear but no complicated stat/class/leveling system that I noticed. Reading into Prison of Husks' Steam page, it sounds like there will be some build differentiation in the weapons and supplemental accessories instead. I'm also happy to report that it runs great out of the box on Steam Deck⁠—even with throwback graphics, that's not always a guarantee a game is actually lightweight enough for the Linux-based handheld. As a bonus, the Deck's 16:10 screen is also a nice fit for Husks' 4:3 aspect ratio. Prison of Husks is planned to launch sometime this year.
